PSK CIRCUIT TROUBLESHOOTING
OBJECTIVES
w Determine if a PSK/QPSK transmitter and receiver system is operating correctly.
w Identify the faulted component in a malfunctioning PSK/QPSK transmitter and receiver system.................
. The experiment in this lesson is not setup to use the selected trainer.
EQUIPMENT REQUIRED
EQUIPMENT REQUIRED
In this lesson, you will troubleshoot faults in a PSK/QPSK transmitter and receiver system.
INTRODUCTIONM
The same process that is used to troubleshoot other signal processing systems is used to troubleshoot PSK/QPSK systems.
You measure the input signal to the modulator and output signal of the demodulator to determine if the system is operating correctly.
If the system isn't working properly, you determine if the fault is in the modulator, transmission medium or demodulator circuits.
Then you troubleshoot the associated circuitry of that system.
In this lesson you will determine if a PSK/QPSK system is operating properly, and if not, determine where the system is faulted. We will then show you what the failed component is.
Let's begin the lesson on PSK CIRCUIT TROUBLESHOOTING.....................

The receiver consists of the components necessary to demodulate PSK/QPSK signals.
To locate a fault you must first determine if the system is working properly.
If the system is faulted, you determine finally which system is faulty.
If you do not have a good signal on the output of the receiver, the system is faulted.
If faulted, you determine if the transmitter or receiver is causing the problem.
If the output of the transmitter is bad, the modulator circuits are causing the problem.
If the output of the transmitter is good, the fault is in the transmission medium or receiver.
If the input to the receiver is bad, the fault is in the transmission medium.
If the input to the receiver is good, the demodulator circuits are faulted.

Once the fault has been located, further oscilloscope or multimeter measurements will isolate the fault to a particular chip or component. Remember, use an analog multimeter to check transistors. Let's start the experiment.
